editorial.summary: Episode 057 supplies the clearest surviving first-person origin story for DVDASA. David begins with his frustration that interviews compress, paraphrase, or redirect his voice. He contrasts an expansive Howard Stern appearance with the production constraints of Barbara Walters's 2012 ABC interview. The interview, New York media tour, outdoor painting, and spray-painted shirt are independently corroborated; alleged staff retaliation, job risk, private phone contact, and charity-auction outcome remain cast recollection or speculation. David then dates a 24-hour video AMA experiment to November 2, 2012. He recalls performing at the Echoplex with Kid Koala, Money Mark, and Dan the Automator before answering questions through rapid video with a large rotating group. A listener in Stavanger later told him that the linked videos no longer worked. David says Vimeo, YouTube, Reddit-linked hosts, and adult platforms had removed or blocked the material. That source loss, together with dissatisfaction over interviews, led him to ask Asa to create an independently hosted, twice-weekly, fully archived show: DVDASA. This is core corpus provenance. Public-name repairs include Mark Spiegler, Jessie Andrews, Daniel Dae Kim, Estevan Oriol, Eric Nakamura, Krondon, Brother Ali, Stacey Adams, Carey Mulligan, Kum Gang San, and the Friday Night Lights and Parks and Recreation characters. Recalled AMA participation remains attributed unless surviving footage or credits confirms it. The episode also contains an unusually meaningful listener letter about disability, hospitalization, teaching, family loss, creativity, and how DVDASA helped. The public archive preserves that impact but withholds the listener's full identity, health dossier, location, and partner. The room's response veers into suicide and disability generalization, a racist stereotype about Filipina women, intrusive follow-up questions, and a hypothetical deadline for abandoning a disabled partner; none becomes guidance. A 2013 claim that Kim Jong-un executed Hyon Song-wol is corrected because she appeared alive on North Korean television in 2014. The second half debates sadness and creative output. David says heartbreak, brief incarceration, and gambling loss restored urgency; Critter and Asa distinguish finding meaning afterward from enjoying suffering. Their distinction controls: trauma, jail, financial loss, impaired driving, and suicidality are not creativity prescriptions or art-investment signals. Private Mexico and Norway partners, former partners, bereavements, Asa's best friend, and Quiet C remain protected. Four empty artifacts are removed, all 2,463 identity windows remain, and named dialogue stays withheld.
